title: Requirements-to-Architecture (ATAM)
description: Kazman's ATAM evaluates architectures against quality-attribute scenarios before building: the architecture faces its requirements in a structured review. Mismatches surface when they're cheap.

demo.code:
import random
random.seed(1001)
# Factory: from requirements, derive components, interfaces, and check acceptance criteria.
reqs=["user login","process payment","send receipt","audit log"]
comps={
 "AuthService": ["login(user, pw) -> token"],
 "PaymentService": ["charge(token, amount) -> receipt_id"],
 "NotifyService": ["send_receipt(user, receipt_id)"],
 "AuditService": ["log(event)"],
}
# every requirement maps to >=1 component; every component exposes >=1 interface
mapping={"user login":["AuthService"],"process payment":["PaymentService"],"send receipt":["NotifyService"],"audit log":["AuditService"]}
ok=all(mapping[r] for r in reqs) and all(len(v)>=1 for v in comps.values())
print(f"requirements={len(reqs)} components={len(comps)} interfaces={sum(len(v) for v in comps.values())}")
for r in reqs: print(f"  {r} -> {', '.join(mapping[r])}")
print(f"acceptance: full coverage + all interfaces defined = {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
print("DEMO_OK")
demo.output:
requirements=4 components=4 interfaces=4
  user login -> AuthService
  process payment -> PaymentService
  send receipt -> NotifyService
  audit log -> AuditService
acceptance: full coverage + all interfaces defined = PASS
DEMO_OK
demo.note: Runnable demo program verified by execution during the database build.

architecture: Scenarios derive from requirements; the architecture is presented against each; risks and trade-offs record. The evaluation report guides revision.
implementation_status: Public method, established (Kazman et al. 2000). Prototype validated in this build (executed 2026-10-21).
